- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slightly rising, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for volatility.  
- In multi-event periods (≥15 events/30d), model often fails to capture event clustering; apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast mean to reflect lagged impact.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model overfits to recent trends; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce noise.  
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, expect mean reversion toward 20–30% of 30d historical range; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0σ below recent high.
